summary: T. R. V. Murti specialized in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his D.Litt. at Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, later serving at Oxford (~1949–1950), Banaras Hindu University (~1953–1967), and McMaster University (~1970).
T. S. Devadoss works in philosophy and Indology. He held posts at the University of Madras, where his affiliation is attested in 1994 and his position as professor is attested in 2008.

T. S. Eliot was a scholar of philosophy and other fields. He studied at Milton Academy, Harvard, Paris, and Merton College under George Santayana and Charles Rockwell Lanman, later holding posts at Birkbeck (~1917–1919) and the University of Chicago (~1950).

T. S. Rukmani specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She held positions at Miranda House (attested 1983–1989) and Concordia University, where she served as Chairperson of Hindu Studies in the Department of Religion (attested 1989).

T. S. Srinivasa Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He held positions at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1972, as professor from 1984 to 1992, and again in 2007.
T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indology scholar who held positions at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested as Pandit in 1993 and as Professor in 2026.

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar specialized in Indology and philosophy. He served as Principal at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Advaita Vedanta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

T. V. Vasudeva works in Indology and philosophy. He has been affiliated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, attested as an Editorial Committee member in 2001 and as Deputy Director in 2026.

T. V. Venkatachala Sastry is a linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Mysore under Harogadde Manappa Nayak, D. L. Narasimhachar, and K. V. Puttappa, and taught at Osmania University and Mysore (professor 1984–1994).

T. Venkatacharya was an Indology scholar. He held an attested post at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East in 1971 and served as a professor at the University of Toronto (attested 1971–1979).

T. W. Rhys Davids worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned a Ph.D. at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, founded the Pali Text Society, and held chairs at University College London, University of London, and Manchester (1904–1915).
T. Y. Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the Mangala Vihara Buddhist Temple and the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Tadao Yoshikawa specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1955–1964), he held positions at Tokai University, Kyoto University (1974; 1984–2000), Ryukoku University (2002), Hanazono University, and the Toho Gakkai (~2007–2011).

Tadashi Inoue specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, holding appointments at Kyoto National Museum (1967, 1979), Nara University (1987), Iida City Museum (1988–2006), Bukkyo University (1995), and Kyoto University of the Arts (2000).

Tadashi Sekino specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1892 to 1895 and later served there as professor emeritus from ~1929 to 1935.

Tadashi Tani works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University, studied at Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama (1995), and taught at National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (attested 1996–2000).
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Skorupski specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of London (1978) and held positions as Professor (attested 1987–1996) and Reader (attested 2005) at SOAS University of London.
Tai-shing Wut works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Ming-Wood Liu (attested 1998).
Taido Kitamura works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held appointments at Shuchiin University, attested as an assistant professor in 1980 and with an attested affiliation from 1994 to 1999.
